title: Low‐dose misoprostol for the prevention of low‐dose aspirin‐induced gastroduodenal injury

sections.abstract: <jats:sec><jats:title>Introduction:</jats:title><jats:p>The harmful effects of non‐steroidal anti‐inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) on the gastric mucosa and the prophylactic effects of misoprostol are both dose‐dependent.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Aim:</jats:title><jats:p>To investigate whether a low‐dose of misoprostol is sufficient to prevent gastric mucosal injury caused by low‐dose aspirin.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Methods:</jats:title><jats:p>We conducted a double‐blind placebo controlled parallel group endoscopic study in 32 evaluable volunteers. The main outcome measure was erosive injury (ulcers and superficial erosions) in the gastric mucosa over 28 days.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results:</jats:title><jats:p>Most subjects developed erosions on aspirin 300 mg daily. This was significantly reduced by misoprostol 100 μg daily. (Odds ratio 0.18, 95% CI: 0.07–0.48). There were no drug‐related or gastrointestinal adverse events in subjects receiving misoprostol.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title><jats:p>Misoprostol 100 μg daily can prevent low‐dose aspirin induced gastric mucosal injury without causing identifiable adverse effects.</jats:p></jats:sec>
